analysis:
This PR changes only documentation: a new changelog entry (changelog.d/gptoss-stop-in-final-channel.md, lines 1-9) and a one-line edit to the `stop` row of the parameter table in docs/architecture/inference.md (changed line ~1846). Neither file contains executable code, so there is no direct change to authorization, attestation, encryption, billing, or data-exposure controls. The text describes a behavior change that lives in source files outside the supplied evidence: GPT-OSS client `stop` sequences now match only the Harmony `final` message, via `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope` and `StopHoldback`, instead of the whole output. I could not verify that implementation. The base_text excerpts of inference.md cover lines 1-805 and do not include the edited table row near line 1846, so I could only check the patch hunk for that row.

Security-relevant observations, for the next pass to confirm against the actual Swift changes:
- Tool-call arguments are described as never cut by stop matching. The tool-call and Harmony frame parsing should be confirmed to be unaffected, so that stop handling cannot truncate or inject tool-call content.
- Stop sequences no longer cut analysis (private reasoning). Reasoning-length bounds should be confirmed to depend on `max_tokens` and cancellation rather than on stop matching, so that DoS exposure under T-010 and T-029 does not grow. A model that never reaches the `final` channel now ends only on `max_tokens` or EOS.
- The docs say the reported stop sequence 'replays the same scope' in `EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift`. Confirm there is no leakage of analysis text into the reported stop sequence or into content.
- The prefix-cache threat T-041 is unaffected by documentation alone.

No concrete security regression is identified from the supplied documentation changes. The behavior itself rests on source not supplied here, so a deeper review is warranted only if the corresponding code changes are in another batch.
